Based in Poole, Dorset. Working remotely across the UK and internationally.

Your brand needs to communicate what you do, who you are for and why someone should choose you. I bring the positioning, words and visual direction together so the identity has a purpose beyond looking good.

BRANDING FOR SMALL BUSINESSES

Start with what the business needs to say.

A logo can be a focused commission or part of a fuller identity. The right starting point depends on whether the business already has a clear name, audience, position and message, or whether those decisions still need work.

I ask about the business, the people it needs to reach and where the identity will be used. That informs the creative direction, rather than choosing a style simply because it is popular.

The aim is a distinctive identity you can use consistently on your website, social profiles, documents and marketing materials. We agree the outputs and intended uses before the design work begins.

What the work can include

  • Brand positioning and direction
  • Business naming and messaging
  • Standalone logo design
  • Colour and typography choices
  • Brand identity and supporting assets
  • Digital and marketing materials

A useful brief makes the design stronger.

Tell me what the business does, who you want to attract and what should feel different about it. Existing materials, references and examples of what you dislike are all useful. You do not need to arrive with a finished design idea.

Once the direction is agreed, the work develops through the review points included in your quote. The deliverables specify the assets and file formats being supplied, along with the agreed revision scope.

Logo or full brand identity?

A logo project focuses on the mark itself. A wider identity can include how colour, type, messaging and supporting elements work together. If you need website design or additional materials as well, we can scope those separately so the costs are clear.

Logo design starts from £100 and brand identity from £250. Naming, additional applications, specialist production requirements and other assets depend on the brief. Design work does not replace legal advice or trade mark clearance.

Before we start.

Can I commission just a logo?

Yes. A standalone logo project starts from £100. The quote defines the deliverables, review process and file formats for your intended use.

Do I need to know the colours and style already?

No. Your audience, business and intended uses give us the starting point. References can help communicate preferences, but you do not need to design the solution yourself.

Can you use an existing brand?

Yes. Send the current logo, available source files and any guidelines. I can assess whether the task is an additional asset, a refinement or a wider identity project.
